places.name: Caernarfon Castle
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, this medieval fortress was built by Edward I and is renowned for its polygonal towers and historical significance. It offers stunning views of the Menai Strait and is a symbol of English dominance in Wales.

opening_hours.notes: Hours vary seasonally; check website before visiting.

places.place_tip: Climb the Eagle Tower for panoramic views of the town and surrounding area.
places.address: Castle Ditch, Caernarfon LL55 2AY, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Caernarfon Castle 1994
attribution.author: Herbert Ortner
attribution.description: Caernarfon Castle, western view at low tide

places.name: Caernarfon Town Walls
places.ai_summary: A well-preserved medieval town wall encircling the historic center of Caernarfon. Built alongside the castle, the walls feature defensive towers and gates, offering a glimpse into the town's strategic importance during the 13th century.

opening_hours.notes: Accessible via various entry points around the town.

places.place_tip: Walk along the walls for unique perspectives of the castle and harbor.

attribution.title: Caernarfon Castle 1994
attribution.author: Herbert Ortner
attribution.description: Caernarfon Castle, western view at low tide

places.name: Doc Fictoria & Waterfront
places.ai_summary: A vibrant waterfront area featuring a marina, shops, cafes, and art galleries. Doc Fictoria is a hub for leisure and culture, offering scenic views of the Menai Strait and a relaxing atmosphere for visitors.

opening_hours.notes: Shops and cafes have individual opening hours.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a sunset drink at one of the waterfront cafes.
places.address: Doc Fictoria, Caernarfon LL55 1TH, United Kingdom

places.name: Welsh Highland Railway
places.ai_summary: A heritage railway offering scenic steam train rides through the stunning landscapes of Snowdonia. The railway connects Caernarfon with Porthmadog, passing through forests, mountains, and along the coast.

opening_hours.notes: Check the website for seasonal variations and special events.

places.place_tip: Book a window seat for the best views and consider a round trip to fully enjoy the scenery.

attribution.title: Gelert locomotive at the Welsh Highland Heritage Railway - August 2018 - 08
attribution.author: nzsteam
attribution.description: Gelert is an 0-4-2T steam locomotive built by W. G. Bagnall in 1953 as No. 3050 and supplied to the Rustenberg platinum mines in South Africa. It is now based on the Welsh Highland Heritage Railway.

places.name: Royal Town of Caernarfon Square
places.ai_summary: The central square of Caernarfon, featuring the iconic statue of David Lloyd George, the town's most famous son. The square is surrounded by historic buildings, shops, and cafes, and often hosts local events and markets.

opening_hours.notes: The square is always accessible; individual shops and cafes have their own hours.

places.place_tip: Visit the local market if you're there on a Thursday or Saturday for fresh produce and local goods.

attribution.title: Britain Before the First World War; Prince Edward, Duke of Windsor Q107152

attribution.description:

Crowds look on as members of the British royal family leave Caernarfon Castle, Caernarfon, Wales, following the Investiture of the Prince of Wales, later King Edward VIII, on 13 July 1911.

places.name: Galeri Caernarfon
places.ai_summary: A cultural and arts venue located in a former warehouse, Galeri Caernarfon hosts a variety of events including concerts, theatre productions, and art exhibitions. It also features a cinema and a cafe.

opening_hours.notes: Check the website for the event schedule and holiday hours.

places.place_tip: Look out for special events or exhibitions that might be taking place during your visit.

places.name: Segontium Roman Fort
places.ai_summary: The ruins of a Roman fort located just outside Caernarfon, Segontium was once a significant military base. The site features well-preserved walls, a bathhouse, and a museum displaying artifacts found in the area.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Sundays from November to March; check website for details.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the small museum on site for a deeper understanding of the fort's history.

attribution.title: Segontium Roman Fort - geograph.org.uk - 1287434
attribution.author: JThomas
attribution.description: Segontium Roman Fort Built around 77A.D. to house 1000 soldiers.

places.name: Llyn Padarn & Llanberis
places.ai_summary: A picturesque lake and village located a short drive from Caernarfon. Llyn Padarn is popular for its stunning scenery, walking trails, and water sports. Llanberis is known for its slate museum and as the starting point for the Snowdon Mountain Railway.

opening_hours.notes: The area is always accessible; individual attractions have their own hours.

places.place_tip: Visit the Slate Museum in Llanberis for a unique insight into the area's industrial history.

attribution.title: Llyn Padarn from Penllyn on a March day - geograph.org.uk - 1768452
attribution.author: Eric Jones
attribution.description: Llyn Padarn from Penllyn on a March day Crib Goch and Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) form the background.

places.name: Dinorwig Quarry
places.ai_summary: The site of a historic slate quarrying operation, Dinorwig Quarry is now a popular spot for walking and climbing, offering dramatic scenery and a glimpse into the area's industrial past.

opening_hours.notes: The site is always accessible; take care when exploring the quarry area.

places.place_tip: Wear sturdy shoes and be prepared for uneven terrain if you plan to explore the quarry.

attribution.title: DinorwicQuarry
attribution.author: nantcoly
attribution.description: Sinc Vivian, Dinorwig Quarries, Wales

places.name: Snowdon Mountain Railway
places.ai_summary: A scenic railway that takes visitors on a journey to the summit of Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales. The train offers stunning views of the surrounding mountains and valleys.

opening_hours.notes: Operates from April to October; check the website for the timetable and availability.

places.place_tip: Book tickets in advance, especially during peak season, to avoid disappointment.
places.address: Snowdon Mountain Railway, Llanberis, Caernarfon LL55 4TT, United Kingdom

places.name: Gypsy Wood Park
places.ai_summary: A unique family attraction set in a magical woodland, featuring life-sized fairy tale scenes, a petting farm, and a narrow-gauge railway. Gypsy Wood Park is designed to delight children and adults alike.

opening_hours.notes: Open from April to October; check the website for exact dates and times.

places.place_tip: Bring a camera to capture the magical scenes and consider a visit to the petting farm.
places.address: Gypsy Wood Park, Caernarfon LL55 2YH, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Natalie Wood Allan Warren
attribution.author: Allan warren
attribution.description: Natalie Wood taken in her London Home in Belgravia.

places.name: St Baglan’s Church Ruins
places.ai_summary: The picturesque ruins of a medieval church set in a tranquil location. St Baglan’s Church is a peaceful spot for reflection and offers beautiful views of the surrounding countryside.

opening_hours.notes: The ruins are always accessible; please respect the site and take your litter home.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with a walk in the surrounding countryside for a relaxing half-day trip.
places.address: St Baglan’s Church, Caernarfon LL55 2AY, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Baglan - geograph.org.uk - 41828
attribution.author: Chris Shaw
attribution.description: Baglan. Viewed from Mynydd Dinas to the SE.

places.name: Anglesey Sea Zoo (nearby)
places.ai_summary: Wales' largest marine aquarium, located on the nearby Anglesey island. The zoo is home to a wide variety of marine life and offers interactive exhibits, a touch pool, and daily talks and feeding sessions.

opening_hours.notes: Open from Easter to October; check the website for exact dates and times.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the daily feeding sessions for a chance to see the animals active and engaged.
places.address: Anglesey Sea Zoo, Brynsiencyn, Caernarfon LL61 6TQ, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Anglesey Sea Zoo - geograph.org.uk - 119361
attribution.author: Lynne Kirton
attribution.description: Anglesey Sea Zoo. Founded in 1983 on the site of an oyster hatchery, Anglesey Sea Zoo is Wales's largest marine aquarium, housing over 50 species from around the Anglesey and N. Wales coastline. Residents include lobsters, sharks, seahorses and conger eels.

places.name: Dinas Dinlle Beach
places.ai_summary: A beautiful sandy beach located a short drive from Caernarfon. Dinas Dinlle is popular for swimming, sunbathing, and picnicking, and offers stunning views of the Snowdonia mountains.

opening_hours.notes: The beach is always accessible; take care when swimming as there are no lifeguards on duty.

places.place_tip: Visit the beach at low tide to explore the rock pools and enjoy a wider sandy area.
places.address: Dinas Dinlle Beach, Caernarfon LL54 5TW, United Kingdom

places.name: Menai Bridge Views
places.ai_summary: Various viewpoints around Caernarfon offer stunning views of the Menai Bridge, an iconic symbol of North Wales. The bridge connects the island of Anglesey with the mainland and is an important piece of engineering history.

opening_hours.notes: The viewpoints are always accessible; take care when parking and walking near the roads.

places.place_tip: There are several great spots for photos; explore a little to find the best angle.
places.address: Menai Bridge, Caernarfon LL57 3LQ, United Kingdom

attribution.title: The Menai Suspension Bridge (35349065306)
attribution.author: Reading Tom from Reading, UK
attribution.description: Built 1818 to 1826 by Thomas Telford completing the London to Holyhead Turnpike Road. Reconstructed 1938-40 by Sir Alexander Gibb, for Dorman Long and Company. The chains were moved from their original central position to their present location and the toll house on the Anglesey side was demolished.

places.name: Parc Glynllifon
places.ai_summary: A beautiful country park located a short drive from Caernarfon. Parc Glynllifon features stunning gardens, woodland walks, and the ruins of a Victorian mansion. It's a great spot for a peaceful walk or a family picnic.

opening_hours.notes: The park is always accessible; individual attractions within the park may have their own hours.

places.place_tip: Explore the walled garden and the remains of the mansion for a glimpse into the area's history.
places.address: Parc Glynllifon, Caernarfon LL54 5DY, United Kingdom

attribution.title: The grand portico of Plas Glynllifon - geograph.org.uk - 304711
attribution.author: Eric Jones
attribution.description:
The grand portico of Plas Glynllifon The Glynllifon estate will always be linked with the notorious Maria Stella (1773-1843), the daughter of an Italian policeman, who at the age of 13 married the middle aged first Lord Newborough in 1786. She bore him two sons. After her husbands' death she moved to Paris where she married a Russian Count. She then laid claim to the throne of France on the grounds that her true father was Louis Philippe, the Duke of Orleans. The present mansion was built by Maria's second son, the 3rd Lord Newborough - Spencer Bulkeley Wynn (1803-88).

http://www.gtj.org.uk/en/subjects/2433

http://www.llechicymru.info/IQPGlynllifon.english.htm

places.name: Doc Victoria Art
places.ai_summary: An art gallery and studio space located in Doc Fictoria, showcasing contemporary Welsh art. The gallery hosts regular exhibitions, workshops, and events, and is a great place to discover local artists.

opening_hours.notes: Check the website for the exhibition schedule and holiday hours.

places.place_tip: Look out for unique handmade items and artwork by local artists.
places.address: Doc Victoria, Caernarfon LL55 1TH, United Kingdom

places.name: Twthill Castle Mound
places.ai_summary: The remains of a medieval castle located on a hill overlooking Caernarfon. Twthill Castle offers panoramic views of the town, the castle, and the Menai Strait.

opening_hours.notes: The site is always accessible; please respect the ruins and take your litter home.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with a walk around the town walls for a complete historical experience.
places.address: Twthill Castle, Caernarfon LL55 2AY, United Kingdom

places.name: Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) Trails (nearby)
places.ai_summary: The trails leading to the summit of Snowdon, the highest peak in Wales, are accessible from Caernarfon. The most popular route is the Llanberis Path, which offers stunning views and is suitable for walkers of moderate ability.

opening_hours.notes: The trails are always accessible; check weather conditions before setting out.

places.place_tip: Start early to avoid crowds and allow plenty of time to enjoy the views and take photos.
places.address: Snowdon Mountain, Llanberis, Caernarfon LL55 4TT, United Kingdom
